context.description: which ranked list this belongs to

priority.description: criticality rank within its context; 1 = most impactful

starting_value.description: schema 1.0 form; a 2.2 record uses typical_values

controls.description: one plain-language sentence saying what the setting is; the page prints it under the title

if_increased.description: schema 1.0 form; a 2.2 record uses effects.increase

if_decreased.description: schema 1.0 form; a 2.2 record uses effects.decrease

common_mistake.description: schema 1.0 form; a 2.2 record uses mistakes

options.description: for a setting with no numeric scale (a switch, a named choice): every value it takes and what choosing it does; drawn as one tile per option in place of the axis

effects.description: what changes when the value goes down or up, as short phrases; drawn as the effect scale

scale.description: the numeric axis of the effect scale; typical_min and typical_max mark the band the typical_values span

value.description: the value as it is written in a configuration, e.g. true, bf16

effect.description: one or two plain sentences: what choosing this value does

typical_value.description: one value somebody used or ships as a default, with the page that states it; a value written as one plain number (0.9, 50, 1e-3) is also marked on the effect scale

setting.description: who used it, and for what

source.description: the url of one entry of this record's sources

schedule_visual.description: the learning rate at every training step, computed by the consumer from these values

peak.description: the value reached at the end of the warmup

final_ratio.description: where the cosine curve ends, as a share of the peak; 0 when absent

marks.description: steps of the worked example, marked on the plot and listed under it

distribution_visual.description: next-token probabilities of one small set of scores, computed by the consumer as softmax(logits). Exactly one of three fields says what is compared: temperatures (one panel per temperature), truncate (before and after candidates are removed) or penalty (before and after the repetition penalty)

logits.description: one score per token, in the same order

truncate.description: which candidates are removed before the draw; the rest are renormalised. Exactly one rule

top_k.description: keep every token whose score is not below the k-th highest score (Transformers TopKLogitsWarper)

top_p.description: keep the most probable tokens up to and including the one whose running total reaches p (Transformers TopPLogitsWarper)

remove.description: tokens of `tokens` whose score is set to minus infinity, as min_new_tokens does to the end-of-sequence token

penalty.description: the repetition penalty as Transformers RepetitionPenaltyLogitsProcessor applies it: a positive score of a repeated token is divided by value, a negative one multiplied by it

repeated.description: tokens of `tokens` that are already in the text

beams_visual.description: a two-step tree of next-token probabilities; the consumer multiplies along each path and marks what greedy decoding and beam search with num_beams each return

tree.description: the candidate first tokens, each with the candidates that can follow it
